inputs.text: They wrapped this man in national-security charges over alleged contact with Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri,” then the Punjab and Haryana High Court said suspicion alone couldn’t justify holding him indefinitely. That looks like the familiar play: use secrecy laws to manufacture fear and make an accusation sound like proof, then retreat once the case can’t sustain the detention. The bail doesn’t settle guilt or innocence—but the timing raises questions about who benefits from keeping the public frightened while the evidence remains uncertain.

subtopics: Suspicion as a basis for detention
